technical_and_design_decisions: Use Go modules to manage the externalized dependencies from the Hyperledger Fabric repository.
Remove the internal and third_party copied code from the SDK repository and replace them with imports from the externalized Fabric packages.
Ensure backward compatibility for SDK consumers by maintaining the same public API interfaces where possible, or documenting any necessary changes.
Implement the temporary go.mod workaround for chaincode packages as a clearly marked, isolated component to facilitate easy removal in the future.
assumptions: The externalized packages in the Hyperledger Fabric repository are stable and provide the required functionality.
The developer has a deep understanding of the Hyperledger Fabric Go SDK architecture and Go modules.
Existing unit and integration tests in the SDK are sufficient to verify the refactoring, though some test updates may be required.
No new features are being added; this is strictly a refactoring and dependency management effort.

activities.activity_description: Review the current internal copies of the utilities, identify the corresponding externalized packages in the Fabric repository, and plan the migration strategy.
Replace the internal modified version of the gossip discovery client and protoext with the externalized copy from Fabric.
Remove the third_party copy of cauthdsl and update the SDK to use the common components from Fabric.
Remove the third_party copy of ccprovider and update the SDK to use the common components from Fabric.
Remove the third_party copy of ledger and update the SDK to use the common components from Fabric.
Replace the internal modified versions of common and core utilities with the externalized copies from Fabric.
Implement the temporary logic to honor go.mod files that are part of a chaincode package during the transition to modules.
Replace the internal modified version of configtxgen functions with the externalized copy from Fabric.
Replace the internal modified version of configtxlator functions with the externalized copy from Fabric.
Run unit and integration tests, fix any breaking changes caused by the refactoring, and ensure the SDK functions correctly with the new dependencies.
